watermark_capacity — IMGFORENSICS watermark op

• Data kinds: image2d × phash → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.watermark_capacity(image, bits, strengths=(0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4), wavelet: 'str' = 'haar', level: 'int' = 1, jpeg_quality=None) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import imgforensics; imgforensics.watermark_capacity(image, bits, strengths=(0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4), wavelet: 'str' = 'haar', level: 'int' = 1, jpeg_quality=None) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsimgforensics.get("watermark_capacity"))

Usage

Sweep the trade-off between embedding strength and PSNR / BER. table.

For each strength it actually runs embed → extract, and returns

psnr_db PSNR between the original and the watermarked image (value range [0, 1] basis, MAX=1)

ber bit error rate of the extraction (counted with hash_distance)

clipped fraction of pixels of the watermarked image that fall outside [0, 1].

The overflow is always lost when saving, so raising the strength looking only at PSNR

increases "degradation you did not measure"

If a quality is passed in jpeg_quality, ber_jpeg, extracted after passing the watermarked image through a real JPEG, is also included (Pillow required. When omitted, the column is absent altogether —— it is not run by default, so that the returned columns do not vary with the environment).

The return is {"capacity_bits": int, "n_bits": int, "rows": [...], "caveats": [...]}.
